title: 2008 Sooners: Five Straight 60-Point Games and a Scoring Record
question: Which Oklahoma team scored 60 points in five straight games?
answer: The 2008 Oklahoma Sooners scored at least 60 points in five consecutive games, capped by a 62-21 win over Missouri in the Big 12 Championship Game. That team scored 716 points, then the Division I single-season record.
summary: The 2008 Sooners scored 60+ in five straight games, capped by a 62-21 Big 12 title win over Missouri, and set a then-record 716 points in a season.
body: The 2008 Oklahoma offense was not just good; it rewrote the record book. Down the stretch the Sooners scored at least 60 points in five consecutive games, something no team had done since Tulsa in 1919.

The run went like this: 62-28 over Nebraska, 66-28 over Texas A&M, 65-21 over Texas Tech, 61-41 at Oklahoma State, and finally 62-21 over Missouri in the Big 12 Championship Game. Five games of 60 or more points in a season is listed as an NCAA record, as is the team's 99 touchdowns.

That title game, played December 6, 2008, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, was a showcase. Quarterback Sam Bradford threw for 384 yards and two touchdowns, setting Big 12 title game records for passing yards and for completions with 34, and the Sooners clinched their third straight conference championship. Along the way, the points pushed OU past Hawaii's 2006 single-season scoring mark of 656.

Oklahoma finished the season with 716 points, the Division I single-season record at the time; Florida State later topped it in 2013. The one thing the offense could not do was finish the job in the BCS National Championship Game, where Florida won 24-14 on January 8, 2009.
Even without the crystal football, the 2008 Sooners remain the measuring stick whenever fans argue about the most explosive offense in program history.
